### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **21** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/validate-list-view-field-refs.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-defaults/ui.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ui/create-vs-edit-form.mdx`  _(via AddRecordConfigSchema (symbol, a top-level const), addRecord (literal, a string literal in sections))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via retiredAfter (symbol, a field of const object addRecordEnabledDefaulted; a field of const object addRecordModeFormViewRemoved), retiredFromLoadPath (symbol, a field of const object addRecordEnabledDefaulted; a field of const object addRecordModeFormViewRemoved))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/validate-list-view-field-refs.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-defaults/ui.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6440cf16334e1c8106dfdb31d87b6ca728d176c2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1fe2d6a94e12ed4f6b9c54c1de3080cfa8983af1` — the merge of head `fc643e459f6327a3840106256a3eb3a6f575a800` into base `6440cf16334e1c8106dfdb31d87b6ca728d176c2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1fe2d6a94e12ed4f6b9c54c1de3080cfa8983af1 && git checkout 1fe2d6a94e12ed4f6b9c54c1de3080cfa8983af1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6440cf16334e1c8106dfdb31d87b6ca728d176c2 fc643e459f6327a3840106256a3eb3a6f575a800 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6440cf16334e1c8106dfdb31d87b6ca728d176c2 && git merge --no-ff fc643e459f6327a3840106256a3eb3a6f575a800

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6440cf16334e1c8106dfdb31d87b6ca728d176c2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6440cf16334e1c8106dfdb31d87b6ca728d176c2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fc643e459f6327a3840106256a3eb3a6f575a800`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.ui__AddRecordConfig__formView.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.ui__AddRecordConfig__mode.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.add-record-enabled-required.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.add-record-mode-form-view-retired.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template, packages/spec/src/ui/page.form.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/view.form.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts (the `interfaceConfig.addRecord` embed at :1060 and the page `list-view` node, read unchanged), packages/spec/scripts/lib/default-changes.ts, packages/spec/authorable-defaults/ui.json, packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json, packages/spec/liveness/view.json, packages/spec/src/shared/retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/add-record-config-retirement.test.ts, .changeset/24692-add-record-retired.md, examples/app-showcase/src/ui/views/contact.view.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/ui/pages/active-projects.page.ts, packages/lint/src/showcase-shape.fixtures.ts, content/docs/ui/create-vs-edit-form.mdx, content/docs/ui/views.mdx; for the landing question only: .github/workflows/ci.yml (`console-pin`), .github/workflows/spec-shape-gate.yml, .github/workflows/release.yml, scripts/build-console.sh, and objectui `packages/types/src/__tests__/p1-spec-alignment.test.ts`, `packages/types/src/objectql.ts`, `packages/types/src/index.ts`, `packages/types/tsconfig.json`, `packages/types/tsconfig.test.json`, `packages/types/package.json` at the pin `616df6598b` and at objectui `main` `cf153eb2e5`.

Read against: card #24692 (body; ruling 6281834942 letter B′ items 1–6; seat-2 hold 6282077441; the 甲 note 6292027850; dispatch 6296388083; dev reports 6299365608 and 6303362402), the standing ruling #6015 comment 6292005854 (「甲」), the PR body, its 37-file list and the three-dot diff `origin/main...fc643e459f`, and the head's check-runs. This head supersedes the record's first reading at `a05f141642` (FAIL on `Test Core (3/6)`): the delta between the two net diffs, taken by explicit sha, is one merge of `origin/main` (no content of this PR's) and one line in `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/object-lifecycle-panel-echo-decisions.test.ts` — the zh-CN positive control `673 → 677`, with a provenance comment — which is exactly the four `addRecord.*` row labels this PR authored in all three locales being counted as translated. No schema, conversion, form, bundle, producer or docs byte moved between the two heads, so every judgment below stands as read on the first head.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change, named against the ruling:

1. **`enabled` REQUIRED, no default — right (ruling item 1).** `view.zod.ts` replaces `.default(true)` with `z.boolean({ error })` whose prescription fires only on `issue.input === undefined`; a non-boolean value gets zod's own type refusal (the new test pins both channels). `addRecord: {}` is refused at every door that embeds the def. `AddRecordConfig` is `z.input`, so the omission is also a `tsc` error at authoring (test `fails tsc at the authoring site when enabled is omitted`).
2. **`position` default `bottom` → `top` — right (ruling item 1).** Values unchanged. `DEFAULT_CHANGES_BY_MAJOR[18]` carries the move; `authorable-defaults/ui.json` regenerated (`enabled`/`mode` rows gone, `position = "top"`). No conversion writes `position`, and that is the correct call: an omitted position rendered at the top before and after, and the 18.0 parse materialised `bottom` explicitly into built artifacts, which keep it.
3. **`mode` / `formView` retired — right (ruling item 2).** Both are `retiredKey()` tombstones on the strict object (input type `never`, parse refusal carries the prescription with the house `os migrate meta --from 17` sentence); `authorable-surface/ui.json` marks both `[RETIRED]` in the file's existing spelling; `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR[18]` gains `ui/AddRecordConfig:mode` and `:formView` (the two `retired-keys/18.*` entries); D2 `add-record-mode-form-view-removed` strips both keys with one notice per key (fixture: 7 notices across all four doors); D3 `add-record-mode-form-view-retired` and its step-18 rationale fragment are present; `retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts` joins both tombstones and the `enabled` refusal under `retiredAfter: '18.0.0'`, which is the newest published stable (`packages/spec/package.json` reads 18.0.0 on `main`).
4. **Every schema that embeds `AddRecordConfigSchema` — right.** On `main` the def is embedded at `view.zod.ts:3116` (`ListViewSchema`, from which `ObjectListViewSchema` and the page `list-view` node's props row derive) and `page.zod.ts:1060` (`InterfacePageConfigSchema`). One def, so the tombstones and the required key reach all of them without a second edit. The conversion walker `mapAddRecordBlocks` reaches the same set: `stack.views[]` in all three persisted spellings via `mapViewPayloads` (kind `list` only — form payloads correctly untouched), `objects[].listViews.*`, `pages[].interfaceConfig`, and every page component of `type: 'list-view'` via `mapPageComponents`. The new test replays a stored view container, a stored page (both page doors) and a stored object through the strict doors; the pin test's walked-shape check keeps the `[RETIRED]` rows reachable.
5. **Forms — right.** `view.form.ts:178` and `page.form.ts:165` composites now spell `fields: [{ field: 'enabled' }, { field: 'position' }]`; the four locale bundles gain the two nested labels (generated, `check:i18n` in the gate set). The liveness ledger row records the removal on the parent (the sub-keys are one drill level below a recorded undrilled container, so no row is added or removed — correct).
6. **Producers and docs — right (ruling item 3).** `active-projects.page.ts:36`, `contact.view.ts:60` and `showcase-shape.fixtures.ts:414` lose both keys; `create-vs-edit-form.mdx:88` states the convention and names no binding; `views.mdx` no longer teaches `addRecord.formView`. The convention the docs now state is live at the pin: objectui `recordFormNavigation.ts` at `616df6598b` carries the objectui#13099 selection ("Which record flow a form view is selected for"), so the docs do not run ahead of the vendored renderer.

**The `add-record-enabled-defaulted` conversion under 「甲」 rule 1 — within the derivation, no escalation owed.** The triage derivation (6292027850) and the dispatch (6296388083) both name the exact alternative: "the PR either carries a conversion that writes the old default (`true`) onto an authored `addRecord` that omits it, or that half ships as a warning in 18.x and its refusal is filed for 19.0 — the dev decides from the measurement and says which." The PR takes the first branch and says so. Judged on the rule's own terms:
- *Lossless against the contract:* yes. The written value is exactly what the 18.0 parse produced for the same body (`.default(true)`), so a converted row means what the published spec said it meant; it is idempotent (a converted block carries `enabled`, never touched again) and deliberately narrow (an explicit `false`, `null` or a non-boolean is left to the parse).
- *The pixel consequence* (a stored block that omitted `enabled` drew no Add button because the renderer read the raw body, and now draws one) is the consequence of the branch triage prescribed — writing `true` is writing the button — not a choice the dev added. It is stated in the changeset, the D3 entry, the `DEFAULT_CHANGES` reason and the conversion docblock, with the one-line remedy (`enabled: false` or drop the block). The measured population is zero in this repo and in objectui's Studio design surface at the pin; production databases were not measured, and the PR says so. The alternative branch (warning now, refusal in 19.0) would have left `addRecord: {}` silently drawing nothing for another major, which is the trap the ruling's facet ③ exists to close. So: derivation honoured, honestly stated, no behaviour change beyond what the ruling and triage already decided.

Also read, nothing wrong found: the `--from 17` wording in the prescriptions is the house sentence `retiredKey`'s docblock pins; `retiredFromLoadPath: true` on both D2s means a live author meets the tombstone while stored rows, built artifacts inside their floor window and `os migrate meta` replay them (the `RetiredConversionState` contract); the two conversions are ordered 72 then 73, strip before default, so a block that carried only `mode` still gets `enabled: true` written after the strip; the old `view.test.ts` / `page.test.ts` pins on `mode` and the `bottom` default are rewritten rather than deleted.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset** `.changeset/24692-add-record-retired.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/lint: patch`; title `feat(spec)!:`; `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`; `**BREAKING**` paragraph with the FROM → TO table and the one-line fix. `packages/platform-objects` (generated i18n bundles) and the showcase are covered: platform-objects is in the same `fixed` group as spec in `.changeset/config.json`, the showcase is an example. `Check Changeset` concluded success.
- **What publishes vs what the level says:** a published schema narrows (required key, two tombstones) and a parsed default moves. Under the standing ruling 「甲」 rule 1 a narrowing an ADR-0087 conversion carries ships in an 18.x minor; `minor` is therefore the ruled level, and the prescriptions' "since @objectstack/spec 18.1.0" matches the next minor off 18.0.0. The `Clause-②:` line on the PR body (`yes (narrowing: …)`) and on the changeset (`yes (narrowing)`) agree.
- **ADR-0087 registration/disposition:** the changeset carries `adr-0087: registered add-record-mode-form-view-removed, add-record-enabled-defaulted, add-record-mode-form-view-retired, add-record-enabled-required` — the two D2 ids and the two D3 ids, matching the registry, the `retired-keys/` and `semantic/` entries and the two `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragments. The disposition section names the D2s, the D3s, the `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR[18]` rows and the `DEFAULT_CHANGES_BY_MAJOR[18]` moves. The registration gate's conclusion on this head is the verdict on that registration (the `Lint ·` family on the head concluded success).

### ③ Boundary flags

**Gate verdicts on this head (the check-runs ARE the verdicts).** 42 check-runs on `fc643e459f`, every one completed: 36 success, 6 skipped (the full-battery jobs on a `pull_request` event: Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Verify CLI, the dogfood shard, Temporal Conformance, and the two opt-in workflows), 0 failure. `Test Core` and all six shards, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, the whole `Lint ·` family (ESLint, the ADR-0087 registration gate, `check:i18n`) and every `Type Check ·` job concluded success. On the previous head `a05f141642`, `Test Core (3/6)` was red on `@objectstack/platform-objects` (`object-lifecycle-panel-echo-decisions.test.ts`, "zh-CN positive control: expected 677 to be 673"): the control counts genuinely translated `.label` leaves per locale and rose by exactly the four `addRecord.*` row labels this PR authored in zh-CN / ja-JP / es-ES (已启用 / 位置, 有効 / 位置, Habilitado / Posición), so the fix is the pinned count with its provenance line, and no schema, bundle or form byte moved. The dev's second report (6303362402) reproduced the red locally before the fix (`1 failed | 81 passed`) and the green after (`82 passed`, 1232 tests), with the spec and lint batteries unchanged. One process note, answered: the first head's battery had not run `pnpm --filter @objectstack/platform-objects test`, which is why the gate saw it first; the second head's did.

**Dev flag 1 — `active-projects.page.ts` sets `userActions.addRecordForm: false` beside `addRecord: { enabled: true }`, so objectui's `showAddRecord` memo likely withholds the button the page's comment promises.** Answered as pre-existing: `addRecordForm: false` is on `main` before this PR and the PR changes neither key; the page still parses and validates. Not a blocker here. Escalated to the dispatching seat: file a showcase card (carrier: none today) or decline on the record.

**Dev flag 2 / the landing hazard — objectui `packages/types/src/__tests__/p1-spec-alignment.test.ts:189` expects `addRecord.mode` `'inline'`.** Determined from the workflows and the objectui files at the pin; the premise of the question is narrower than feared:
- *What the row is.* The test is type-only against objectui's OWN `ListViewSchema` interface (`packages/types/src/objectql.ts:3038`: `addRecord?: { enabled?: boolean; position?: string; mode?: string; formView?: string }`, a hand-written local shape, identical at the pin and at objectui `main` `cf153eb2e5`). It assigns an object literal and reads `.mode` back; nothing is parsed through `@objectstack/spec`, and the literal is not typed as the spec's `AddRecordConfig` (which objectui re-exports from `@objectstack/spec/ui` at `index.ts:1428` but does not use for this interface). So neither the spec's tombstone (`z.input` of `mode` becomes `never`) nor the required `enabled` reaches that file. It goes red only when objectui itself re-types the interface or re-pins the row, which is what ruling item 4 says happens on objectui's side.
- *Console Pin Gate (`ci.yml` `console-pin`).* Full battery only: `if: event != pull_request && != merge_group`, so it never runs on a PR or a queue build (it reads `skipped` on this head). On the `push` to `main` it also needs the `console` path filter, which lists `.objectui-sha`, `scripts/build-console.sh`, the two check scripts, the probe scripts, `packages/spec/package.json`, `packages/spec/tsup.config.ts` and six other manifests; this PR moves none, so the push run skips it. On the hourly `schedule` (filter forced `true`) it restores the console dist by a cache key over those same inputs — unchanged here — so it hits and the build step is skipped; what runs is `check:console-sha` and `check:console-injection --require-stamp`, which replay the probes stamped at build time against the dist on disk, by the ruled cache design (the spec's content lag behind a cached dist is deliberate). On a miss, `scripts/build-console.sh` only builds (`turbo run build` on the console's deps, then the SPA's own vite build) — it never runs objectui's `vitest`, and objectui's `packages/types/tsconfig.json` excludes `**/__tests__/**` and `*.test.ts` from the build program, so the test is not even compiled there. `release.yml` on the `main` push runs the same build script under a narrower cache key. Nothing in this repo's workflows runs objectui's test suite.
- *Spec Shape Gate (`spec-shape-gate.yml`).* Hourly on `main` (plus `workflow_dispatch`, and `pull_request` only for its own three files); type-checks objectui `main` — chained test projects included (`tsconfig.test.json` is in `packages/types`' `type-check`) — against the spec built from the commit. For the named row: no diagnostic, for the reason above (local interface). Residual, not a finding: any objectui site that types a literal as the spec's `AddRecordConfig` and writes `mode`/`formView` or omits `enabled` would red that hourly run; the dev reports a `git grep` at the pin found no source writing either key, and this review could not enumerate objectui's uses of `AddRecordConfig` from the brief's inputs. Under that gate's own rule a red is the lane's first work plus a one-line registration in `scripts/ci/spec-shape-retirements.json` (the PR does not pre-register, and none is owed before a diagnostic exists); it is a main-red the release gate reads, not a merge blocker.
- **Finding: merging this PR turns no `main`-or-queue job red on the named row. No precondition (objectui change or pin bump) is needed to land; the parity row changes on objectui's side when its pin takes this spec release, as ruling item 4 already binds.**

**Out-of-scope / remaining items from the dev report**, each answered or escalated:
- ADR-0050 Decision 2 dated note (ruling item 5, Tier H): not in this PR, by the choice item 5 grants; the exact one-line text is in the dev report. Escalated to the dispatching seat: dispatch the one-line Tier H PR so the ruling's item 5 does not go unowned.
- Surfaces beyond the claim's file list (default-changes.ts, vitest.repo-tests.json, the migrations entries, registry.ts.template, the pin test, view/page tests, the new test, the liveness README, views.mdx, the two lint files, the i18n bundles, the regenerated references): all declared in the report, all required by the kit; none is a governed path (the `Governed Surface Queue Guard` concluded success). Answered.
- Production databases not measured for `addRecord` blocks omitting `enabled`: stated in the PR, the changeset and the conversion docblock; the conversion is the safe branch for that unknown (no refusal of stored data). Answered.
- Repo-wide `pnpm lint` left to CI: the `Lint · ESLint` check-run on the head is that measurement. Answered.
